organizations.name: NASA
organizations.summary: Through the Artemis program, NASA aims to return humans to the Moon and build a sustained presence at the lunar South Pole as a stepping stone to Mars.

organizations.name: SpaceX
organizations.summary: SpaceX is developing Starship as a fully reusable launch and landing system; a Starship Human Landing System variant is contracted to land Artemis astronauts near the lunar South Pole.

organizations.name: Blue Origin
organizations.summary: Blue Origin is building the Blue Moon lunar landers (MK1 cargo and MK2 crewed) and researches in-situ resource use, including making solar cells and oxygen from lunar regolith.

organizations.name: ICON
organizations.summary: ICON is developing Project Olympus, a multi-purpose lunar construction system that 3D-prints infrastructure — landing pads, roads, habitats — from local regolith, under a NASA SBIR Phase III contract within the MMPACT project.

sources.label: NASA — NASA, ICON advance lunar construction technology

organizations.name: Redwire
organizations.summary: Redwire is prototyping Mason, a platform-agnostic tool suite (grader, compactor, microwave sintering emitter) that turns lunar regolith into solid berms, landing pads, and roads, under a NASA Tipping Point award.

sources.label: Redwire — $12.9M NASA award for lunar infrastructure

organizations.name: Astroport Space Technologies
organizations.summary: Astroport develops the Lunatron/Brickbot induction furnace-nozzle that melts lunar regolith into interlocking bricks for landing pads, roads, and blast shields, advanced through multiple NASA SBIR/STTR awards with UTSA.

sources.label: NASA SBIR — Induction Furnace-Nozzle for lunar regolith bricks

organizations.name: AI SpaceFactory
organizations.summary: AI SpaceFactory, winner of NASA's 3D-Printed Habitat Challenge, is developing regolith-polymer additive construction with NASA Kennedy Space Center (REACT), including the LINA lunar outpost concept targeted at the Shackleton crater region.

organizations.name: Intuitive Machines
organizations.summary: Intuitive Machines leads the Moon RACER team developing an unpressurized Lunar Terrain Vehicle for NASA's LTV Services contract, building on its Nova-C lunar lander heritage.

organizations.name: Lunar Outpost
organizations.summary: Lunar Outpost leads the Lunar Dawn team developing the Lunar Voyager LTV for NASA's LTV Services contract, drawing on its MAPP rover flight experience.

organizations.name: Venturi Astrolab
organizations.summary: Venturi Astrolab develops the FLEX (Flexible Logistics and Exploration) rover, a modular lunar terrain vehicle competing in NASA's LTV Services contract.

organizations.name: Westinghouse
organizations.summary: Westinghouse, partnered with Aerojet Rocketdyne, is developing a lunar surface fission reactor based on its eVinci heat-pipe microreactor for NASA's Fission Surface Power project. NASA and the DOE selected Westinghouse to continue its design in January 2025, competing against Lockheed Martin and the IX (Intuitive Machines–X-energy) team.

sources.label: Westinghouse — NASA-DOE contract for space microreactor

organizations.name: Firefly Aerospace
organizations.summary: Firefly Aerospace flies the Blue Ghost lunar lander under NASA's CLPS program. Blue Ghost Mission 1 made the first fully successful commercial soft landing on the Moon in March 2025 and operated a full lunar day.

organizations.name: Astrobotic Technology
organizations.summary: Astrobotic builds the Peregrine and Griffin lunar landers plus CubeRover mobility, delivering payloads to the surface under NASA's CLPS program.

organizations.name: ispace
organizations.summary: ispace develops the HAKUTO-R and APEX lunar landers and is pursuing a commercial cislunar transport and resource-prospecting business from Japan and the United States.

organizations.name: Sierra Space
organizations.summary: Sierra Space builds inflatable LIFE habitats and a carbothermal reduction reactor that extracts oxygen from regolith, targeting both pressurized volume and in-situ consumables.

organizations.name: Lunar Resources
organizations.summary: Lunar Resources develops molten regolith electrolysis reactors that split raw regolith into oxygen and structural metals, plus in-situ manufactured power infrastructure.

organizations.name: Lockheed Martin
organizations.summary: Lockheed Martin builds the Orion crew vehicle, leads one of NASA's three fission surface power design teams, and owns Crescent Space, its lunar communications and navigation venture.

organizations.name: Thales Alenia Space
organizations.summary: Thales Alenia Space has built a majority of the pressurized volume ever flown on the ISS and is under contract to the Italian Space Agency for the Multi-Purpose Habitat, Italy's surface habitat contribution to Artemis.

organizations.name: JAXA
organizations.summary: Japan's space agency is providing the crewed pressurized rover for Artemis, developed with Toyota, in exchange for two Japanese astronaut flights to the Moon under a 2024 agreement with NASA.

organizations.name: Nokia Bell Labs
organizations.summary: Nokia Bell Labs adapted terrestrial LTE/4G for the lunar surface under a NASA Tipping Point award and flew the first cellular network to the Moon aboard Intuitive Machines' IM-2 in 2025.

organizations.name: European Space Agency
organizations.summary: Through the Moonlight initiative ESA is procuring a shared lunar communications and navigation constellation, with the SSTL-built Lunar Pathfinder relay as its precursor.

organizations.name: Crescent Space Services
organizations.summary: Crescent Space, a Lockheed Martin venture founded in 2023, is building Parsec — a commercial lunar communications and navigation service sold to agency and private missions.

organizations.name: CNSA / Roscosmos
organizations.summary: China's National Space Administration and Russia's Roscosmos are jointly developing the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS), a robotic-then-crewed base aimed at the lunar South Pole, open to partner nations and developed independently of Artemis.

sharedGoals.title: First demonstrated lunar landing-pad construction system
sharedGoals.description: Soft regolith and lander plumes threaten every sustained surface operation — hardened landing pads, roads, and berms are the first infrastructure any base needs. Multiple companies are racing this capability with genuinely different technology bets: laser/large-scale printing (ICON), microwave sintering (Redwire), molten-regolith bricks (Astroport), and regolith-polymer printing (AI SpaceFactory). A future MoonDAO DePrize would reward the first team to meet the frozen capability criteria below.
sharedGoals.regionLabel: Lunar South Pole — candidate construction zone

criteria.statement: Produce a continuous load-bearing surface from lunar regolith simulant
criteria.threshold: ≥ 25 m²; ≥ 90% regolith feedstock by mass

criteria.statement: Survive a published plume / mechanical load profile
criteria.threshold: MoonDAO-frozen spec derived from NASA/ESA plume-surface interaction data

criteria.statement: Demonstrate the process in a relevant environment
criteria.threshold: Vacuum and/or lunar thermal extremes; exact bar frozen at market open

criteria.statement: Publish an open performance data pack for peer review and simulation use
criteria.threshold: Strength, thickness, energy per kg, dust shedding

criteria.statement: Quote a CLPS-class flight demonstration within budget
criteria.threshold: Quote ≤ prize-pool TWAP at market close

market.budgetGate: Winning team's CLPS-class flight-demo quote must not exceed the prize-pool TWAP at market close.

sources.label: NASA — NASA, ICON advance lunar construction technology (MMPACT)
NASA — Tipping Point partnerships (incl. Redwire Mason)

sharedGoals.title: First commercial crewed lunar landing
sharedGoals.description: NASA's Human Landing System program put two competing landers under contract: SpaceX's Starship HLS (Artemis III) and Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK2 (Artemis V). Which system puts crew on the lunar surface first is the defining near-term race in the lander tech tree — schedules on both sides have moved, and each vehicle still has major flight-test milestones ahead.
sharedGoals.regionLabel: Lunar South Pole — Artemis candidate landing zone

sources.label: NASA — Blue Origin selected for Artemis V lander

sharedGoals.title: First sustained crewed South Pole presence
sharedGoals.description: Two publicly declared programs are building toward a permanent crewed foothold at the lunar South Pole, on independent tracks: NASA's Artemis Base Camp (habitats, power, and mobility, following the Artemis III crewed landing) and the China–Russia International Lunar Research Station (ILRS), built up through robotic phases toward crewed utilization from 2036. The crewed landers that ferry astronauts down for each program are raced separately in the lander tech tree.

criteria.statement: Establish continuous crewed occupancy at a fixed South Pole site
criteria.threshold: ≥ 2 weeks continuous stay, repeated across multiple missions

criteria.statement: Demonstrate closed-loop life support beyond a single sortie
criteria.threshold: Regenerative O2/water systems operating in situ

criteria.statement: Power the site from local generation sized to sustained base load
criteria.threshold: Solar or fission surface power, not primary batteries or a single sortie's fuel cells

sources.label: SpaceNews — China, Russia reveal roadmap for international moon base

sharedGoals.title: First sustained oxygen and metals from lunar regolith
sharedGoals.description: Oxygen is most of the mass of a lunar propellant load and all of the mass of a breathable atmosphere, and hauling either from Earth caps how large a base can get. Blue Origin makes solar cells and oxygen by molten regolith electrolysis, Sierra Space pulls oxygen out carbothermally, and Lunar Resources runs molten regolith as its own electrolyte to get metals alongside the oxygen.

criteria.statement: Produce oxygen from regolith at a sustained rate
criteria.threshold: ≥ 1 kg O₂ per day continuous, ≥ 90% regolith feedstock by mass

criteria.statement: Run the process in a relevant environment
criteria.threshold: Vacuum and lunar thermal extremes; exact bar frozen at market open

criteria.statement: Publish energy cost per kilogram of product
criteria.threshold: kWh per kg O₂, measured end to end including feedstock handling

criteria.statement: Demonstrate endurance rather than a single batch
criteria.threshold: Continuous or repeated operation across ≥ 100 hours

sharedGoals.title: First crewed lunar terrain vehicle in service
sharedGoals.description: NASA's LTV Services approach put the unpressurized lunar rover out to industry. Three teams — Intuitive Machines (Moon RACER), Venturi Astrolab (FLEX), and Lunar Outpost's Lunar Dawn (Lunar Voyager) — completed feasibility work, and NASA will issue a demonstration task order for a crew-capable rover at the South Pole. Which vehicle reaches operational service first is the rover tech tree's race.
sharedGoals.regionLabel: Lunar South Pole — Artemis operating area

sharedGoals.title: First operational fission surface power on the Moon
sharedGoals.description: Nothing else carries a base through the 14-day lunar night. NASA and the Department of Energy funded three 40 kWe reactor designs in 2022 — Lockheed Martin with BWXT and Creare, Westinghouse with Aerojet Rocketdyne, and IX, the Intuitive Machines and X-energy joint venture — and in 2025 directed the program to accelerate toward a 100 kWe reactor launching by 2030. The three teams started from identical contracts, which makes this the closest-run race on the board.

criteria.statement: Deliver continuous electrical power through a full lunar night
criteria.threshold: ≥ 40 kWe for ≥ 354 hours without solar input

criteria.statement: Operate without crew intervention on the surface
criteria.threshold: Autonomous start-up, load-following, and safe shutdown

criteria.statement: Qualify for a decade of surface operation
criteria.threshold: 10-year design life demonstrated by test and analysis

criteria.statement: Fit a single lander delivery
criteria.threshold: Mass and envelope within one human-class lander manifest

sources.label: NASA — NASA, DOE select design concepts for fission surface power

sharedGoals.title: First pressurized habitat occupied on the lunar surface
sharedGoals.description: Three different bets on where crews will actually live. Thales Alenia Space is building Italy's rigid Multi-Purpose Habitat for delivery around 2033; Sierra Space argues for inflatables that launch folded and expand on site; and Japan's Lunar Cruiser makes the first habitat a vehicle, keeping two crew unsuited for a month while it drives. Whoever gets there first defines what a lunar home is.
sharedGoals.regionLabel: Lunar South Pole — Artemis Base Camp

criteria.statement: House crew on the surface at habitable pressure
criteria.threshold: ≥ 2 crew living unsuited for ≥ 14 consecutive days

criteria.statement: Close the loop on air and water well enough for the stay
criteria.threshold: Life support sustained without resupply for the demonstrated period

criteria.statement: Keep the volume habitable through a lunar night
criteria.threshold: Thermal and power margin across a full 354-hour night

criteria.statement: Support expansion rather than standing alone
criteria.threshold: Berthing or docking interface for a second pressurized element

sources.label: NASA — NASA, Japan announce crew rover agreement

sharedGoals.title: First operational lunar communications and navigation service
sharedGoals.description: Every mission today flies its own radio link back to Earth, which does not scale to a base. Four groups are trying to make connectivity something you buy: Nokia has already run LTE on the surface, Intuitive Machines holds NASA's Near Space Network relay contract, ESA is procuring the Moonlight constellation behind its Lunar Pathfinder relay, and Lockheed's Crescent Space is selling Parsec as a subscription.
sharedGoals.regionLabel: Lunar South Pole — service coverage area

criteria.statement: Carry a third party's mission traffic, not just the operator's own
criteria.threshold: ≥ 1 external customer mission served operationally

criteria.statement: Cover the south-pole operating area including permanent shadow
criteria.threshold: Published availability over the Artemis exploration zone

criteria.statement: Provide position and timing, not only a data link
criteria.threshold: Surface positioning fix to a published accuracy

criteria.statement: Interoperate under the LunaNet framework
criteria.threshold: Conformance to NASA/ESA LunaNet interoperability specifications
